guidance.inspection: Reconstruct the complete operative definition of protected information, including incorporated definitions, list introductions, alternatives, exclusions, and form or identification conditions. For explicit identification, Entailment requires every protected item to be identified by the disclosing party; an express alternative such as reasonable understanding, the nature of the information, circumstances, or automatic inclusion is genuine opposing evidence, while silence about marking is only missing support. For technical-only scope, identify the actual protected subjects: express inclusion of business, financial, marketing, customer, personnel, operational, or similar nontechnical information opposes the hypothesis; generic breadth or an unrelated definition does not. For verbal information, require language including oral or verbal communications, even if later identification or written confirmation is required; a written category that says nothing about oral information does not by itself establish exclusion. Preserve the governing definition, each decision-bearing alternative, necessary preambles, and independently operative definitions; reject nearby use, disclosure, return, and negotiation clauses that do not define protected information.

For each issue, locate an operative permission, exclusion, restriction, or reservation and identify actor, action, information object, purpose, recipient class, and every condition. Independent development requires development or derivation without using, accessing, or referring to protected information; third-party acquisition requires receipt from a source other than the discloser with lawful provenance and no confidentiality duty. Do not substitute one exception for the other. Employee sharing and nonemployee sharing each require an operative disclosure or access permission; retain any incorporated definition and need-to-know, purpose, undertaking, consent, and responsibility conditions. A recipient-class definition or incidental actor mention is missing support, while an exclusive employee-only permission can oppose nonemployee sharing. Limited use requires a rule confining use of protected information to the stated purpose; purpose-qualified copying or disclosure is not enough, and an express broader internal-business or residuals permission is opposing evidence. No-licensing requires an express no-right, no-license, ownership, or reservation rule concerning protected information; evaluation access or purpose-limited use neither grants a right nor opposes the hypothesis. Retain all independently operative responsive clauses and their governing lead-ins without importing unrelated candidates.

Read every return, destruction, copying, retention, and survival provision in its complete clause structure. For return or destruction upon termination, the same operative duty must connect the receiving party, protected information, mandatory return or destruction, and a termination, expiration, rejection, conclusion, abandonment, or comparable end trigger; a request-at-any-time duty does not qualify merely because another clause separately permits termination. Copy permission requires an affirmative necessary-purpose exception, copies required for authorized use, or an acknowledged automatic copying process. A bare prohibition subject to possible consent is opposing evidence under the observed labels, not affirmative permission. Post-return possession requires an express exception allowing identified material or copies to remain after the governing return or destruction duty, with holder, purpose, access, duration, and continuing-confidentiality limits. A duty covering all material and copies without such an exception is opposing evidence; archival persistence without permission is insufficient. Survival requires language continuing an identified obligation after termination, expiration, completion, abandonment, return, or destruction; a termination right, retention exception, or accrued-remedies clause alone is missing support. Preserve the governing trigger, alternatives, exceptions, list preambles, cross-references, and every independently operative or repeated responsive provision.

Inspect the full document for four distinct operative controls. Agreement confidentiality requires a nondisclosure duty covering the agreement or its existence or terms, or the existence, content, status, or terms of discussions or negotiations; when coverage comes from a protected-information definition, retain both that definition and the governing secrecy duty. Ordinary references to an agreement or transaction are missing support. Compelled-disclosure notice requires legal, regulatory, governmental, subpoena, court, or administrative compulsion to trigger notice, information, or consultation to the disclosing party; retain timing, legal-permission qualifications, and any protective-order mechanism. Unauthorized-use notice or bare compelled-disclosure permission does not suffice. No-solicitation requires the receiving party to refrain from soliciting identified personnel or representatives; retain target class, action, duration, consent condition, and exceptions, and exclude proxy solicitation or unrelated standstill language. Reverse engineering requires an operative prohibition on the receiving party reverse engineering, decompiling, or disassembling an object embodying protected information; general secrecy, copying, product-use, or intellectual-property language is not equivalent. An express affirmative authorization would be opposing evidence, but no located clause or candidate is only missing support. For every issue retain necessary preambles and independently operative responsive provisions, and do not treat examples or candidate retrieval as proof of whole-document absence.
